title: Project Data Structures
description:
Define core data structures for project representation.

Structures to implement:
- ProjectType enum: Rust, Node, Python, Flutter, JavaMaven, JavaGradle, Cpp, DotNet, Go
- Project struct with fields:
  - name: String (derived from config file or directory name)
  - project_type: ProjectType
  - path: PathBuf (project root)
  - artifacts: Vec<PathBuf> (directories/files to delete)
  - total_size: u64 (bytes)
- Config struct for user options from CLI

Traits:
- Display for ProjectType (icons/labels)
- Size calculation helpers

acceptance_criteria:
- ProjectType enum covers all 9 ecosystems
- Project struct holds all required metadata
- Size calculation is accurate and thread-safe

title: Python Detection
description:
Detect and clean Python project artifacts.

Detection (any of):
- pyproject.toml
- setup.py / setup.cfg
- requirements.txt
- Pipfile / poetry.lock

Artifacts to clean:
- __pycache__/ (all occurrences within project)
- .pytest_cache/
- build/
- dist/
- *.egg-info/
- .tox/
- .coverage files
- venv/ or .venv/ (virtual environments - large but recreatable)

Notes:
- Virtual environments are included by default but user may want to exclude
- Find all __pycache__ directories recursively within project

Source: prd.md - Python section
acceptance_criteria:
- Detects projects with Python config files
- Removes all __pycache__ recursively
- Removes build/, dist/, *.egg-info/
- Removes venv/.venv if present
- Removes test caches

title: Error Handling Strategy
description:
Implement consistent error handling across the application.

Requirements:
- Use Rust Result and Error patterns
- Non-fatal errors logged and continued (don't panic)
- Permission denied: skip with warning
- Locked files: skip with warning
- Descriptive error messages for users
- Exit code 0 on success, non-zero on major failure

Error categories:
- Scan errors (permission denied, missing paths)
- Deletion errors (locked files, permissions)
- Config errors (invalid arguments)

Source: prd.md - Non-Functional Requirements & Error Handling section
acceptance_criteria:
- Errors don't crash the program
- Clear error messages displayed
- Appropriate exit codes
- Warnings for skipped items

title: Deletion Module
description:
Implement safe deletion of build artifact directories.

Requirements:
- Use fs::remove_dir_all for recursive directory deletion
- Proper error handling (continue on permission denied, locked files)
- Non-fatal errors logged and reported, not panic
- Progress feedback during deletion
- Optional parallel deletion (with IO consideration)
- Symlink handling: remove symlink, not target
- Report partial deletions as warnings
- Compute total space freed

Safety:
- Verify path matches expected patterns before deletion
- Never follow symlinks outside target tree
- Log each deletion in verbose mode

Source: prd.md - Deletion Functionality section 2 & Deletion Module section 6
acceptance_criteria:
- Directories deleted recursively
- Errors handled gracefully without crash
- Partial deletions reported
- Symlinks handled correctly
- Space freed reported accurately

- Calculate artifact sizes (optionally parallel)

- Modest memory footprint (stream traversal)

title: Two-Factor Detection Heuristics
description:
Implement safety heuristics requiring both config file AND artifact directory.

Two-Factor Rule:
- Signal A: Config/manifest file present (Cargo.toml, package.json, etc.)
- Signal B: Artifact directory present (target/, node_modules/, etc.)
- Both must be present to identify a cleanable project

Safety benefits:
- Won't delete "build" folder without build config file
- Won't act on config-only projects (nothing to clean anyway)
- Dramatically reduces false positive risk

Edge cases:
- Stray artifact dir without config: ignore (unless --include forced)
- Config without artifact: skip (nothing to do)

Source: prd.md - Safety and Heuristic Mechanisms section
acceptance_criteria:
- Both config AND artifact required
- Random "build" dirs without config ignored
- Config-only projects skipped
- Clear rationale in verbose mode
